tier_rationale: Manufacturer's own product page lists no Bluetooth, WiFi, or app capability for this compressor nebulizer, and no FCC intentional-radiator grant exists for the NE-C801 despite OMRON Healthcare holding 27 grants for other radio-equipped models (its Bluetooth blood pressure monitors), which establishes the vendor files when it has a radio to declare.
the_unplug_test: There is no radio to unplug from anything but the wall. It is an AC-powered air compressor that pushes medication through a nebulizer cup and mouthpiece; you switch it on, breathe, switch it off. No app, no pairing, no account, and nothing about a treatment is recorded anywhere but your own memory.

repairability.notes: Sold with 4 replacement air filters included and a standard nebulizer kit/mouthpiece/air tube that are consumable, vendor-replaceable parts. No teardown checked.

sources.supports: Manufacturer product page: no Bluetooth, WiFi, or app integration mentioned; unit is AC-adapter powered (no battery), ships with a nebulizer kit, mouthpiece, air tube, 4 air filters and instruction manual. A standard tabletop compressor nebulizer with no connectivity of any kind.

FCC ID search for grantee OMRON HEALTHCARE Co., Ltd. (grantee code Q6Z) lists 27 grants, all Bluetooth/BLE blood pressure monitors. No grant exists for the NE-C801 or any OMRON nebulizer model, and the vendor demonstrably files grants for its own radio-equipped products, making the absence for this model meaningful.

open_questions: Current US price band not established.
OMRON also sells a portable battery-operated MicroAir NE-U100 nebulizer and a kids' CompAir RE-C800KD; neither was checked and both are presumed similarly unconnected but unverified.
notes: Fills an empty subcategory (nebulizer) in the health domain with a mainstream, easy-to-buy device rather than a niche one.
